facility: Rittenhouse Boulevard Pump Station and Force Main, West Norriton Township, Pennsylvania
source: Gilmore & Associates, Rittenhouse Boulevard Pump Station capacity study for West Norriton Township, November 2020 (public record)
question: Township operating record (from the client, not in the visible pages): the existing 18-inch cast iron force main broke in the past at an operating pressure of about 90 psi. The Rittenhouse Boulevard sewage pump station must convey the projected 20-year peak flow of 4,960 gpm (7.14 MGD) with one pump out of service. Can the existing station and force main do it? If not, what limits it, and what are the least-cost alternatives (pumps, impellers, force main) that achieve at least 4,960 gpm with two pumps operating? Verify each alternative's operating point.

collection.question: Can the existing Rittenhouse Boulevard pump station and 18-inch cast-iron force main convey the projected 20-year peak flow of 4,960 gpm (7.14 MGD) with one pump out of service? If not, what limits it, and what are the least-cost alternatives (pumps, impellers, force main) that achieve at least 4,960 gpm with two pumps operating? Verify each alternative's operating point.

rfi.issue: Break-pressure limit not in visible pages
rfi.item: Allowable operating pressure for existing 18-in C.I. main
rfi.reason: Only source is Township operating record via brief (~90 psi break); no page gives pressure rating or safety factor, yet pressure governs whether higher-head pumps can use existing main
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: ~90 psi is a hard upper limit for flow in existing C.I. main; any run requiring >=90 psi in existing main fails — reason: conservative use of only break evidence to avoid repeat failure; verify by run_hydraulics pressure output

rfi.item: Whether 3,200 gpm required two pumps or all three pumps
rfi.reason: p.3 says with two pumps operating (2016 Rettew inspection) while p.4 says with all three pumps operating (1992 test); cannot both describe same current condition
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: treat both as dated historical observations, not as current firm capacity; decide capability by hydraulic operating point from p.10/p.13 data — reason: system/pump curves give testable current basis

rfi.reason: Text sum vs Table 1 total differ by 11 gpd; 7.14 MGD converts to ~4,958 gpm, not exactly 4,960 gpm
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: govern by 4,960 gpm / 7.14 MGD / 7,141,500 gpd stated need — reason: difference is negligible (<0.001 MGD) and brief fixes 4,960 gpm as pass threshold

rfi.issue: Alternative pump / impeller / force-main details withheld

rfi.reason: Available pages include only existing 17.25-in curve (p.13) and existing main (p.10); withheld pages contain recommendations; study must still identify least-cost paths
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: develop alternatives from facts (retain structure, change rotating equipment first, then main) and verify each by run_hydraulics referring to labelled runs; any new pump-curve or new-pipe numbers introduced later will be labelled ASSUMPTION with reason — reason: instruction says withheld clauses require own conclusions from facts
